comment: Static IL patches applied to the player's sts2.dll by Spire.Patcher (tools/build_logic.py). Each replaces a Harmony patch from sts2-cli; handlers for 'redirect' ids are in logic/Spire.Logic/Hooks.cs. A missing non-optional target fails the build: that is the signal the game API moved (see docs/LOGIC_BUILD.md).

patches.note: Cuts the game logic off from its Godot UI layer: every call from logic into a UI class (namespace MegaCrit.Sts2.Core.Nodes.*, or any game class deriving from a Godot class, e.g. NDebugAudioManager) becomes a recorded presentation cue (sound, VFX, speech, music) with a safe default result. A singleton getter (NCombatRoom.Instance) heading a ?. chain that is a statement of its own returns a stand-in instead of null, so calls such as Instance?.PlaySplashVfx(...) or Instance?.CombatVfxContainer.AddChildSafely(NThinSliceVfx.Create(...)) are recorded rather than skipped; chains that dereference or keep a UI result outside the UI keep the null (Spire.Patcher IsStatementUiChain).

The Godot UI layer never runs headless (the 'ui' patch redirects every call into it). Method bodies of the Godot-derived classes there (nodes, and what is nested in them) become a throw so the AOT builds do not compile the UI (console code size). Constructors stay, and plain helper classes in those namespaces (EpochComparer) are untouched. A 'headless: ...' NotSupportedException in a log means the logic reached UI code.

Game logic calls into Godot engine objects (scenes from the asset cache, tweens, nodes) that are null without the engine. A null receiver now skips the call with a safe default; non-null receivers (stub objects) behave as before.
Game code awaits Task.Delay for pacing (e.g. Amalgamator). A real timer would leave the adapter reporting a decision mid-effect; every call completes at once and records a 'wait' cue instead.

UI animation delays. Completes at once (no scene tree) and records a 'wait' cue with the duration, which the presentation uses for pacing (sts2-cli: PatchCmdWait).
The fast / standard wait (the turn banners' 0.8 s, ...). It skips itself headless (NonInteractiveMode under TestMode); the hook records the wait the game's FastMode setting would make.

OnPlayWrapper ends a play with CustomScaledWait(0.15 - elapsed, 0.3 - elapsed), elapsed by Time.GetTicksMsec since the play started. Headless the effects take no time, so the clock is the waits recorded meanwhile (Steps.ClockMs): a play waits only what its effects did not.
CardPileCmd.Add awaits the tween of its cards changing piles; TestMode makes none. The hook records the time it would run (a draw's 0.25 s, Fast 0.1, ...) and returns no tween, as TestMode does.
The discard pile's size as Shuffle starts: its cards fly to the draw pile min(0.045, 0.8 / n) s apart (card.shuffle_tween).
Shuffle waits between the cards it flies to the draw pile (NCardFlyShuffleVfx), which it skips when TestMode makes no tween. Recorded as those waits; no tween is returned.
AddDuringManualCardPlay awaits a power card's move to the play pile (0.25 s) before the hook; the hook records it and calls Hook.AfterCardChangedPiles.
RemoveFromCombat burns a card that has a node (in the hand, or played and not a power) with NCardExhaustVfx; headless there is none. Recorded as card_burn cues before the cards leave their piles.

CardModel.EnqueueManualPlay runs the card's OnEnqueuePlayVfx (a ground fire, the PowerUp animation) alongside the play it queues. Headless it runs inline: Steps.BeginBranch keeps its waits off the turn's timeline.
The end of card_enqueue_vfx's branch.

A relic's DoActivateVisuals (Flash, IsActivating, Cmd.Wait(1)) runs alongside the effect that triggered it (TaskHelper.RunSafely). Headless it runs inline: Steps.BeginBranch keeps its waits off the turn's timeline.
The end of relic_activate's branch.
InfestedPower reveals the Wrigglers after the elite's death animation, alongside the turn. Headless it runs inline: Steps.BeginBranch keeps its waits off the turn's timeline.
The end of infested_reveal's branch.
StockPower reveals the replacement after the death animation, alongside the turn. Headless it runs inline: Steps.BeginBranch keeps its waits off the turn's timeline.
The end of stock_reveal's branch.
ReattachPower's fade of the segments, alongside the turn. Headless it runs inline: Steps.BeginBranch keeps its waits off the turn's timeline.
The end of reattach_vfx's branch.
Lord's Parasol buys the merchant's stock one item after another, alongside entering the shop. Headless it runs inline: Steps.BeginBranch keeps its waits off the turn's timeline.
The end of lords_parasol's branch.
Creature.SetNodeVisible sets the creature node's Visible (a Godot setter, not recorded): recorded as a node_visible cue (InfestedPower hides the Wrigglers until the elite's death animation is over).

OnPlayWrapper's replays: from the second play on, a card that is not a power plays NCard.AnimMultiCardPlay (FindOnTable finds no node headless). Recorded as a multi_play cue and its CustomScaledWait(0.4, 0.5).

A power card's swoop into its owner (NCardFlyPowerVfx) and the wait on it. Headless NCard.FindOnTable finds no node, so the original would wait CustomScaledWait(0.1, 0.8) for a new card instead; recorded as the game plays a card from the play pile.

CardPileCmd.RemoveFromDeck(cards, showPreview): the card grows in and burns away (NCardRemoveVfx). Recorded as deck_card remove cues.
CardCmd.Upgrade(cards, style): its preview style, for the deck cards it upgrades (deck.upgraded).
The end of CardCmd.Upgrade(cards, style).
A card upgraded inside CardCmd.Upgrade: a deck card gets NCardUpgradeVfx in the style's container. Recorded as a deck_card upgrade cue.

NEventRoom's VfxContainer gets NRainVfx.Create() (as the mirror). Recorded as its ui cue.

The Sovereign Blade orbiting the player is a node the game finds under the creature (SovereignBlade.GetVfxNode); headless there is none, so every forge looked like a new blade. The adapter keeps which blades exist and records blade cues (forge, orbit) with the forge / refine sound.
The play's target, for the blade's attack (blade.attack_node).
SovereignBlade.OnPlay's BeforeDamage: the blade (vfxNode.Attack) flies at the target. Recorded as a blade attack cue; the call still finds no node.
The blade goes (RemoveSovereignBlade: exhausted, transformed). Recorded as a blade remove cue.

RelicModel.Flash: the Player handler plays the relic's sound (recorded) and gives each target an NRelicFlashVfx, which TestMode's null VFX container skips; the top bar's holder flashes too (NRelicInventoryHolder). Recorded as a relic_flash cue.
PowerModel.Flash: only UI subscribers (NCreature's NPowerFlashVfx, NPower's icon particles). Recorded as a power_flash cue when the power would play its VFX.

RollingBoulderPower.AfterPlayerTurnStart: TestMode damages every hittable enemy at once; the game rolls NRollingBoulderVfx over them and damages each as it passes (its HitCreature signal). The hook plays that branch: the boulder's cue, then each enemy's own damage after a boulder_hit mark the client times by the boulder's path.

See power.pulse_start.

The adapter runs the game with TestMode on, and some rules depend on it: a new profile's first act is an undiscovered alternate act (ActModel.GetRandomList), shop potion prices vary by +/-5% (MerchantPotionEntry, a Shops RNG draw), bosses and encounters follow the discovery order and a first run's unknown rooms are events (RunManager's tutorial rules), the run history records HP and gold per floor and reloads are counted, Calling Bell offers a common, an uncommon and a rare relic and Cauldron random potions (TestMode: fixed test ones), and leaving a shop records what it had left in the run history (MerchantRoom.Exit). Runs that follow the game's own flow (start_game_run) see TestMode off at exactly these sites; other runs see the real value, unchanged.
See testmode.game_flow.is_off.

VfxCmd.PlayNonCombatVfx(container, position, path): an event's effect at a position in its room (Dense Vegetation, Jungle Maze); null in TestMode, which Dense Vegetation then sets a rotation on. Recorded as a ui cue (the path and the position); a stand-in Node2D comes back.
RunSaveManager.SaveRun raises Saved, which NSaveIndicator.SavedGame answers (GAME_SAVED fades in and out in the top bar's corner). Recorded as a saved cue.

ForgeCmd.PreviewSovereignBlade (after a Forge): NCardSmithVfx on each Sovereign Blade in the hand, and one showing the others before they fly back to their piles; no sound. It returns at once in TestMode. Recorded as a forge_preview cue.

Foul Potion thrown at a merchant out of combat: NMerchantRoom.FoulPotionThrown (thank-yous, a foulPotion line, a rumble) or NFakeMerchant.FoulPotionThrown (its line before the fight), with vfx_slime_impact at the merchant button (ShowPotionVfx). NRun.Instance is null headless, so the shop's never run. Recorded as a foul_potion cue.

Lord's Parasol at a shop buys every item one by one (cards, relics, potions, 0.25 s apart), then the card removal; the decision after it shows them all sold. Recorded as a shop_entry cue: the shop as entered, for the client to play the purchases on.

MerchantEntry.InvokePurchaseCompleted: NMerchantInventory.OnPurchaseCompleted animates the slot (a card to the deck, a relic or potion to the top bar). Recorded as a merchant_purchase cue (kind, index), auto when no buy command made it (Lord's Parasol).

DollRoom.BeforeEventStarted's ambience (NDebugAudioManager.Play): recorded as a cue; TestMode reads on (the handle it keeps stays null).

SandpitPower (The Insatiable) moves its target towards the owner as it counts down, from where the target stood when it was applied (Godot positions, TestMode on: nothing). Recorded as Sandpit.Begin, Sandpit.Update (with the tween's 0.25 s) and Sandpit.Pull cues.
See sandpit.applied.

SandpitPower.AfterRemoved's TestMode-off reads: the first pulls everyone it holds in, each later one hides one of their bodies (cues queued by sandpit.removed); TestMode reads on.

AttackCommand's custom hit effects (WithHitVfxNode). A lambda's Create call is redirected like any UI call, but a UI method bound directly as the delegate (WithHitVfxNode(NBigSlashVfx.Create): Sovereign Blade, Grand Finale, Gunk Up, the Wrigglers) would run its stripped body. The hook registers the delegate wrapped: such a method's call is recorded instead.
See attack.hit_vfx_node: the attacker's custom effects (WithAttackerFx(Func<Node2D>)).

VfxCmd.GetSideCenterFloor is null in TestMode, and End of Days makes its NLargeMagicMissileVfx (and waits its WaitTime) only with a position. Answered with a position the client resolves as the game computes it (eN@side_floor: the side's hittable creatures' mean bottom x, their lowest bottom).

VfxCmd.GetSideCenter is null in TestMode; the Mecha Knight's hit effects take its .Value (an exception once they run). Answered with the side's first creature's centre, encoded as the stand-ins' positions are, so the effect is recorded at it.

Presentation the game skips in TestMode, with no effect on the rules: the potion thrown from the player to its target (NItemThrowVfx, then a 0.5 s wait), the rest site's healing cross, and the monsters' calls on their special nodes (the Myte's and Snapping Jaxfruit's targets, the Flyconid's spore kind); the Tunneler's attack from below (sound, animation, 1 s), Vantom's charge-ups (waits, sounds, its track-1 animations, the music's progress), the Waterfall Giant's build-up (music, ambience, track-1 animation; its PressureBuildupIdx only decides whether its body fades after death), the elites' second-phase music (Bygone Effigy, Infested), Bouncing Flask's throws and splashes (0.5 s each), Hand of Greed's target position for its coins. TestMode reads off there in every run, so it reaches the steps as cues (the UI calls stay redirected).

DecimillipedeSegment.AnimSegmentsAttack plays its rocks the way VfxCmd.PlayFullScreenInCombat does (the scene at the screen's centre in the combat VFX container), written out in the move. The scene lookup becomes the same 'vfx at screen' cue; it returns null as the asset cache does headless.

Creature.GetCreatureNode returns null in TestMode; in every run here it reaches the UI stand-ins (NCombatRoom.GetCreatureNode, NBestiary.GetCreatureNode), so the monsters' calls on their creature nodes become cues. Creature.GetVfxContainer / GetBackVfxContainer likewise answer the room's stand-in containers: the game writes container?.AddChildSafely(X.Create(...)), whose effect is not even made when the container is null (the block spark and Blocked text, heal numbers, every attack's custom hit effect: Shiv, Claw, Perfected Strike, ...). DecimillipedeSegment.AnimSegmentsAttack: the segments' AttackShake (special nodes) and the rocks scene (its asset is null headless, so nothing is made in the logic) before a 0.5 s wait. Presentation only: the nodes are stand-ins whose calls are redirected.
